thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx error rate observed on /v1/generate (us-east-1) — error budget burn. auto-page: @oncall-shift · 3378912345

incident-bot: metrics snapshot: 5xx spike from 0.2% -> 12% in the last 3m. p50 latency up 20%.

sara: I’m seeing gateway 502/504s across multiple customers, correlation to model-runner pods crashing with SIGSEGV in the runtime. Paging in.

mike: @sara on it. I’m pulling logs from the impacted node pool now. Which model(s) are most affected?

sara: Mostly customer workloads hitting redwood/open-llama-70b variants and our largest quantized variants. Fewer errors on smaller backoffs.

alice: Confirming pods restarting rapidly: kube events show OOMKilled then SIGSEGV in the same container. Example container id: `containerd://a7f3d2`

alice: attaching a short log tail:
```
[2026-03-15T14:32:08Z] runtime: MODEL_RUNNER: serving request id=bb9f...
[2026-03-15T14:32:09Z] runtime: kv_cache: miss; starting forward pass
[2026-03-15T14:32:09Z] runtime: gpu-mem: allocated 31824MB (peak)
[2026-03-15T14:32:10Z] runtime: fatal error: segfault at 0x0
[2026-03-15T14:32:10Z] runtime: signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code=1, fault addr=0x0
[2026-03-15T14:32:10Z] core dumped: /var/preserve/cores/runner-core-..
```

dena: interesting — allocation hit the GPU ~31.8GB. Those nodes are A100-40GB. Possibly a kernel-level OOM when loading attention kernels for long sequence lengths.

mike: taking an initial mitigation: enabling fallback routing to `open-llama-13b-quant` for traffic that would hit the 70B variants. Pushing routing change now (route: latency-priority -> cost/availability fallback). Will post command.

mike: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/v1/routing/adjust -d '{"rule":"fallback:open-llama-13b-quant","scope":"us-east-1","percent":100}'` -> 202 Accepted

incident-bot: ROUTE CHANGE applied: %100 fallback to open-llama-13b-quant for requests matching model family open-llama-70b (us-east-1).

alice: early telemetry shows error rate dropped from 12% -> 3% within 45s after route change. Some customers still see sporadic 5xx for pinned model versions.

sara: Good. On-call handoff: @oncall-shift I’ll keep driving live debug for the pods themselves. Can you own customer comms/PG?

oncall-shift: Taking customer comms. Posting status page update: "Investigating elevated errors for generation API in us-east-1; temporary fallback to smaller model; reduced error rate but partial impact for pinned models. ETA next update 20m." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

james: I’m collecting core dumps from the nodes and starting an isolated reproduce run against the same model with identical sequence lengths and batch sizes. Will attach gdb backtrace if it reproduces.

james: quick gdb snippet from the core (strip and anonymized):
```
#0  0x00007f2b3c1a5f9a in attention_forward (ctx=0x7f2c8, args=0x0) at kernels/attn.cu:124
#1  0x00007f2b3c1b11ed in run_layer (layer=42, state=0x7f2c9) at runner/layers.cc:88
#2  0x00007f2b3c1c2abc in forward_pass (config=...) at runner/engine.cc:402
#3  0x00007f2b3c1d4f3e in handle_request (req=...) at runner/server.cc:216
```
Notably `args` or `req->kv` is null here.

dena: that matches a bug we saw in last quarter where a rare race could free KV cache buffer while another thread was reading. Did we recently increase concurrency or change batching?

sara: Yes — we shipped a micro-optimization in release 1.23.4 that moved KV eviction earlier to reduce memory pressure. Could be a regression.

mike: For live mitigation, suggestions: revert micro-optimization in the running image (hotpatch), or reduce `max_prefetch` concurrency and force single-threaded KV access via env var. Which is faster?

alice: Hotpatch requires a rollout of a new image and will take 8-12m to build + deploy. Changing env var via DaemonSet patch to disable async eviction should be immediate-ish (kube rollout not needed) — we can set `KV_EVICT_ASYNC=false` on the node pool config and restart pods slowly.

mike: I’ll apply the env var to the deployment as a temporary toggle and restart one AZ at a time. Command: `kubectl set env deployment/model-runner KV_EVICT_ASYNC=false -n prod --record`

mike: applied to deployment replica set; initiating rolling restart `kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-runner -n prod --max-unavailable=1`

alice: restarting pods in az-a now. Monitoring.

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager noise reduced but not eliminated. Some older pinned model containers still restart due to pre-existing memory fragmentation.

james: After setting KV_EVICT_ASYNC=false and restarting an instance, the runner process stayed up under similar load for 10m in my replicate. No segfault observed.

sara: That’s promising. Keep rolling. Also adding a temporary policy in the gateway to cap request length to 2048 tokens for the impacted model family to avoid worst-case memory allocations.

mike: Gateway cap applied (policy id: gw-cap-3378).

oncall-shift: Customer comms updated: "Mitigation: traffic rerouted to smaller model; we applied runtime toggle and gateway token cap; error rates falling and continuing to monitor. Impact: degraded latency for some high-throughput customers and pinned 70B customers may still see errors. Next update in 30m."

alice: After rolling restart across AZs and routing + gateway caps in place, global 5xx has returned to baseline ~0.4%. We should continue to hold the `KV_EVICT_ASYNC=false` setting until we merge a safe fix.

dena: For the post-incident plan: 1) revert the micro-optimization in 1.23.4 and run stress tests with long sequences 2) add safer null-checks in attention kernel wrapper 3) add a runtime guard to reject requests that would allocate >36GB on A100-40GB nodes 4) add obs metric for KV pointer lifetime to alert earlier.

james: I’ll open a PR with a failing test from reproduce run + core dump analysis. Assigning to eng-runtime.

sara: Thanks team. Current owner for mitigation is eng-runtime (mike + alice + james) to ship hotfix. oncall-shift owns customer comms until all impacted customers are verified.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: Mitigated -> degraded service, monitoring. Paging cleared for on-call.

sara: We should schedule a 1h postmortem meeting tomorrow and include SRE, runtime, and product to validate the customer impact numbers and rollout checklist.

oncall-shift: Schedule sent. Closing thread when postmortem doc is published. :white_check_mark:
